book.title: The Great Arizona Orphan Abduction
book.summary: "In 1904, New York nuns brought forty Irish orphans to a remote Arizona mining camp, to be placed with Catholic families. The Catholic families were Mexican, as was the majority of the population. Soon the town's Anglos, furious at this "interracial" transgression, formed a vigilante squad that kidnapped the children and nearly lynched the nuns and the local priest. The Catholic Church sued to get its wards back, but all the courts, including the U.S. Supreme Court, ruled in favor of the vigilantes."--BOOK JACKET. "The Great Arizona Orphan Abduction tells this disturbing and dramatic tale to illuminate the creation of racial boundaries along the Mexican border."--BOOK JACKET.

argument.statement: The events in Arizona around 1904 show how racial boundaries along the Mexican border were created, including through vigilante kidnapping of Irish orphans and court rulings favoring those actions.
